facets.text: Warsh's hawkish hike supports higher front end rates and twist flattening of the UST curve.
The sharp shift in Fed pricing was catalyzed by the Warsh Jackson Hole (JH) speech and stronger labor and inflation data.
facets.why: One causal claim split by cause

facets.text: Chairman Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks, together with current market pricing, have raised the cost of disappointing expectations significantly.
There is only one additional employment report and one CPI release before the October meeting.
facets.why: Same predicate, split by data release

facets.text: The headline and core inflation projections for 2026 are marked down by roughly 30bp.
The headline and core inflation projections for 2027 are revised down by 0.1pp.
The Warsh Jackson Hole speech was more transparent about Warsh's outlook and Warsh's reaction function.
A larger market move likely comes from a dovish hike or a Fed hold.
Bond yields are lower due to downside growth and inflation risk.
Bond yields are higher due to dovish Fed action and confusion about Warsh policy direction or reaction function.
Twist steepening comes from a lower near term policy path and a perceived very high bar to hike.
Long end rates reflect a higher inflation risk premium and a Warsh credibility discount.
Warsh, others at the Fed, and the Trump admin understand bond risk with a Sept hold.
Bessent and Warsh effectively explain to Trump the tradeoff between tolerating modestly higher front end rates and materially higher long end rates.
Trump understands the risks of bond un-anchoring and its market implications.
Lower growth and inflation risk supports UST investor confidence.
Sept '15, Oct '15, June '23 and July '26 are the 4 closest historic parallels.
There is no change in IORB or ON RRP within range.
Growth and inflation forecasts are elevated even in the context of further hike guidance.
